results.title: The Text Anonymization Benchmark (TAB): A Dedicated ...
results.content: Text anonymization, defined as the task of editing a text document to prevent the disclosure of personal information, currently suffers from a shortage of privacy-oriented annotated text resources, making it difficult to properly evaluate the level of privacy protection offered by various anonymization methods. The corpus comprises 1,268 English-language court cases from the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) enriched with comprehensive annotations about the personal information appearing in each document, including their semantic category, identifier type, confidential attributes, and co-reference relations. TAB consists of a collection of 1,268 court cases from the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) in which each personal information expressed in the documents is explicitly annotated and associated with various properties, such as its semantic category, identifier type, confidential attributes, and co-reference relations. Each annotated text span is associated with the annotator name, its offset in the text, a semantic category, the identifier type (direct, quasi, or no need to mask), possible confidential attributes, and an unique identifier for the entity it refers to (based on the relations from Step 4).12.

results.title: Inside the Great AI Data Grab — Comprehensive Analysis ...
results.content: # *Inside the Great AI Data Grab — Comprehensive Analysis of Public and Proprietary Corpora Utilizsed in Training Contemporary Foundation Language Models*. ## From Common Crawl to Instagram Reels — An Empirical Review of Provenance, Bias, and Regulatory Implications. > *tl;dr — Executive* — LLMs ingest trillions of tokens from five dominant sources: web crawls, reference works (e.g., Wikipedia), books, scientific & code corpora, and social/user-generated text. Public datasets such as Common Crawl and The Pile still anchor most models, but incumbents now blend in licensed or proprietary content (e.g., Meta’s Facebook/Instagram posts, xAI’s X fire-hose) that stays undisclosed for IP, privacy, and competitive reasons. > *Technical* — State-of-the-art models (GPT-4, Claude 3, LLaMA-4, DeepSeek-67B, Grok-1) each exceed 2 T tokens after aggressive filtering (language ID, license & PII removal, MinHash de-duplication). ## Written by Adnan Masood, PhD. Dr. Adnan Masood is an Engineer, Thought Leader, Author, AI/ML PhD, Stanford Scholar, Harvard Alum, Microsoft Regional Director, and STEM Robotics Coach.

results.title: The Ethical AI Bombshell That Just Blew Up Big Tech's ...
results.content: For years, Big AI players like OpenAI and Meta claimed it was impossible to train high-performing models without stealing data. Built entirely from licensed, public, and opt-in data, it trained an open 7B model that performs on par with—or outperforms—the most hyped models released by the Big AI Bros. For years, Big AI’s central claim was that building high-performance models ethically was impossible. Common Pile v0.1 is an 8-terabyte large language model training dataset constructed entirely from legally obtained, ethically sourced content. The result is the first dataset of its size and diversity built on full legal compliance and ethical transparency—designed to prove that performant AI models can be trained without violating copyright, privacy, or consent. Constructed over a two-year period by researchers from EleutherAI, MIT, Cornell, the University of Toronto, and a coalition of academic and open-source partners, the dataset is a technical and ethical landmark: 8 terabytes of text, entirely composed of content that is public domain, openly licensed, or explicitly opt-in.
